decisions.choice: the fifth vision: a gold lampstand fed by two olive trees, with a word for Zerubbabel
decisions.reason: Zechariah sees a lampstand of gold with seven lamps, kept supplied with oil from two olive trees beside it (verses 2-3, 11-12). In the middle of the vision comes a word for Zerubbabel the governor: the temple will be finished not by human strength but by the LORD's Spirit (verses 6-10). The angel explains the seven lamps as the eyes of the LORD (verse 10) and the two trees as two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth (verse 14).

decisions.choice: like someone roused from sleep: Zechariah is stirred to full attention
decisions.reason: The prophet is not said to have fallen asleep, but he was in a state like sleep, and the angel rouses him to see the next vision, as Daniel was roused in his visions (Daniel 8:18; 10:9-10). The angel "came back", as if he had stepped away after the last vision.

decisions.choice: a person / a man; their / his (L); someone (B, R)
decisions.reason: The comparison is with anyone woken from sleep, so Literal gives "a man ... his" the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "someone".

decisions.choice: "como a alguien ... de su sueño", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish can say "alguien" and "su", which cover men and women, so the English gender setting is not needed even at Literal.

decisions.choice: and I said: the form the Hebrew text tells the reader to read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew text have "and he said", and the form marked to be read aloud has "and I said". The reading form fits the dialogue: the angel asks, and Zechariah answers.

decisions.choice: a lampstand of gold with a bowl on top: a lampstand fed from an oil bowl above its lamps
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the seven-branched lampstand of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:31-40), which the priests kept supplied with oil (Exodus 27:20-21). This one is different: a bowl on top holds the oil and feeds the lamps, and the oil comes from two living olive trees (verse 3, 12), not from human hands. The word for bowl is used of a basin or a bowl-shaped lamp (Ecclesiastes 12:6).

decisions.choice: seven and seven spouts: seven spouts on each of the seven lamps
alternatives: seven pipes, one to each lamp
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "seven and seven", a way of saying "seven each". The word translated "spouts" is found only here; it seems to come from a verb for pouring, and may mean the pinched lips of a clay lamp where a wick lay, or pipes carrying oil from the bowl. Clay lamps with seven spouts around the rim have been found in the land of Israel. If so, the lampstand had seven lamps, each with seven flames. Others read seven pipes in all, one to each lamp.

decisions.choice: look (L); spouts (L, B); places for wicks (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order and "look". Balanced and Readable say "each of the lamps has seven", which is what "seven and seven" means (m3), and Readable says what a spout is for. Zechariah's description runs on into verse 3, where the quotation mark closes.

decisions.choice: "un candelabro todo de oro" (L, B), "de oro macizo" (R); "un depósito"; "siete picos" (L, B), "siete lugares para mechas" (R)
decisions.reason: The lampstand, its bowl and its lamps follow the term sheet and 1 Chronicles 28:15 ("candelabro"); "depósito" says that the bowl holds the oil. Zechariah's description stays open and closes in verse 3, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "un chandelier tout en or"; "une vasque"; "sept et sept becs" (L), "sept becs" (B), "sept becs pour les mèches" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the term sheet (Revelation 11:4 has "chandeliers"); the spout of a clay lamp is its "bec". The quotation runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: "kinara cha taa cha dhahabu tupu"; "bakuli"; "midomo saba na saba" (L), "midomo saba" (B), "mahali saba pa kuweka utambi" (R)
decisions.reason: The lampstand of the term sheet; "midomo" are the pinched lips of a clay lamp where a wick lies (m3). The quotation runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: "chân đèn toàn bằng vàng" (L), "chân đèn bằng vàng ròng" (B, R); "cái bầu" (L), "bầu dầu" (B, R); "vòi"
decisions.reason: "Chân đèn bằng vàng ròng" is the lampstand of Exodus 25:31; the bowl is named for the oil it holds. The angel says "ông" to Zechariah. The quotation runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: a word for Zerubbabel inside the vision
alternatives: a passage moved here from elsewhere
decisions.reason: Instead of explaining the lampstand at once, the angel gives a word for Zerubbabel, which runs to the middle of verse 10; then the explanation resumes. Some think these verses once stood elsewhere, but as the text stands the word explains the vision: as the lamps burn with oil that no human hand supplies, the temple will be finished by the LORD's Spirit, not by human strength.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel: governor of Judah and heir of David's line
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel was governor of Judah under the Persians (Haggai 1:1) and led the first group of exiles home with Joshua (Ezra 2:2; 3:2). He was a grandson of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:17-19), so he was of the royal family of David. Haggai calls him the LORD's chosen signet ring (Haggai 2:23). With Joshua he led the rebuilding of the temple.

decisions.choice: might ... power: any human strength, whether armies, wealth or effort
decisions.reason: The first word means strength or ability, and is used for armies and for wealth (Exodus 14:4; Deuteronomy 8:17-18). The second means strength or power in general. Together they rule out every human resource as the means by which the work will be done.

decisions.choice: by my Spirit: by the LORD's own power at work
decisions.reason: The word means wind, breath or spirit, and here it is the LORD's Spirit: his power at work among his people. Haggai 2:5 had promised, "My Spirit remains among you; do not fear." Like the oil that flows to the lamps from the living trees, the Spirit supplies what the builders cannot.

decisions.choice: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, at every level
decisions.reason: The saying keeps one wording at every level, as set for this verse, because readers know it and quote it. "Spirit" is capitalized for God's Spirit, as in Isaiah. The angel's words are in double quotation marks, and the word to Zerubbabel is in single marks inside them; both close at the end of verse 7.

decisions.reason: The saying keeps one wording at every level, as the English does, drafted from the Hebrew as the term sheet asks and kept apart from the familiar Spanish versions. "Espíritu" is capitalized for God's Spirit. The angel's words take « and the word to Zerubbabel “; both close at the end of verse 7.

decisions.choice: the great mountain will become a plain: every obstacle to the rebuilding will be removed
decisions.reason: The mountain stands for whatever stood in Zerubbabel's way. It may be the opposition of the peoples around, which had stopped the work for years (Ezra 4:1-5, 24; 5:3-5), or the great heap of rubble on the temple site, or the sheer size of the task. The text does not say. The picture of mountains made level is used of the LORD's coming in Isaiah 40:4.

decisions.choice: the top stone: the last stone, which marks the building complete
alternatives: the first stone, laid at the start of the building
decisions.reason: The word comes from "head", which can mean the top of something or its first or chief part. If the top stone is meant, Zerubbabel will set the last stone and so complete the temple, as verse 9 says he will finish it. Some read it as the first or chief stone, set when the work began again. The text does not describe the stone more closely.

decisions.choice: Grace, grace to it!: a shout calling down God's favor on the stone
alternatives: How beautiful, how beautiful it is!
decisions.reason: The word means favor or grace, and also charm or beauty. The people's shout may be a blessing on the finished building, asking for God's favor on it, or a cry of delight at its beauty. The first sense fits the theme of the chapter, that the work is done by God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: who do you think you are? (R); the last stone of the temple (R); God bless it! (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a challenge, which is how it is meant, and says which stone is meant and what the shout asks for (m3). "Grace, grace" would mean little to a new reader. The closing marks end the word to Zerubbabel and the angel's words.

decisions.reason: "Piedra principal" keeps the word's sense of head or top without choosing a corner stone (m2); Readable says what the shout asks for, as the English does. The shout sits inside the word to Zerubbabel, so it takes ‘ ’ inside “ ” inside « ».

decisions.reason: The top stone is the one that crowns the building (m2); the nested shout takes ‘ ’ inside “ ” inside « », and all three close here.

fr.R: Zorobabel a posé les fondations de ce temple de ses propres mains, et il l’achèvera de ses propres mains. Alors tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.

sw.L: Mikono ya Zerubabeli imeiweka misingi ya nyumba hii, na mikono yake [itaimaliza]; nawe utajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.
sw.B: Mikono ya Zerubabeli imeweka msingi wa nyumba hii, na mikono yake itaikamilisha. Ndipo utakapojua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.
sw.R: Zerubabeli ameweka msingi wa hekalu hili kwa mikono yake mwenyewe, na kwa mikono yake mwenyewe atalimaliza. Ndipo utakapojua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.

vi.L: Tay Xô-rô-ba-bên đã đặt nền nhà này, và tay người sẽ hoàn tất [nó]; và ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với ngươi.
vi.B: Tay Xô-rô-ba-bên đã đặt nền móng cho nhà này, và tay người sẽ làm xong. Bấy giờ ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với ngươi.
vi.R: Chính tay Xô-rô-ba-bên đã đặt nền móng cho đền thờ này, và chính tay người sẽ xây xong. Khi ấy ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với ngươi.

ko.L: 스룹바벨의 손이 이 집의 기초를 놓았으니, 그의 손이 [그것을] 끝낼 것이다. 그때에 너는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 스룹바벨의 손이 이 집의 기초를 놓았으니, 그의 손이 이 집을 완성할 것이다. 그때에 너는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 스룹바벨이 자기 손으로 이 성전의 기초를 놓았으니, 자기 손으로 그것을 완성할 것이다. 그때에 너는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: founded this house: began building the temple
decisions.reason: Ezra 3:8-10 tells of the foundation laid under Zerubbabel and Jeshua soon after the return, and Haggai 2:18 dates the founding of the temple to the year of this prophecy, 520 BC, when the stalled work began again. The verb can mean the start of the building as a whole. The temple was finished in the sixth year of Darius, 515 BC (Ezra 6:14-15).

decisions.choice: you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me: the finished temple will prove the message true
decisions.reason: The words are the same as in 2:13 and 2:15. When Zerubbabel completes the temple, the people will know that the prophet spoke for the LORD (Deuteronomy 18:21-22). "You" is singular here, perhaps speaking to Zechariah, perhaps to each hearer.

decisions.choice: temple (R); with his own hands (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "house" and makes the point of "his hands" plain: the man who began the work will finish it himself. Literal says "you shall know", as in 2:13 and 2:15.

decisions.choice: "sabrás ... a ti", singular, with no plural_you
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew "you" is singular (m2), unlike 2:13, so Spanish says tú.

source.text: כִּ֣י מִ֣י בַז֮ לְי֣וֹם קְטַנּוֹת֒ וְשָׂמְח֗וּ וְרָא֞וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֧בֶן הַבְּדִ֛יל בְּיַ֥ד זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעָה־אֵ֑לֶּה עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הֵ֥מָּה מְשׁוֹטְטִ֖ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: For who has despised [the] day of small things? And they will rejoice and see the stone the tin in [the] hand of Zerubbabel. These seven [are] the eyes of Yahweh; they range in all the earth.

en.L: For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven [are] the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they range through all the earth.
en.B: Who has despised the day of small beginnings? People will rejoice when they see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel's hand. These seven are the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which range over the whole earth.
en.R: Some people looked down on the work because it began so small. But they will be glad when they see Zerubbabel holding the plumb stone. These seven lamps are the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which look over the whole earth.

es.L: Porque ¿quién ha menospreciado el día de las cosas pequeñas? Se alegrarán y verán la piedra de estaño en la mano de Zorobabel. Estos siete [son] los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; ellos recorren toda la tierra.
es.B: ¿Quién ha despreciado el día de los comienzos pequeños? La gente se alegrará al ver la plomada en la mano de Zorobabel. Estos siete son los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que recorren toda la tierra.
es.R: Algunos despreciaron la obra porque comenzó muy pequeña. Pero se alegrarán cuando vean a Zorobabel con la plomada en la mano. Estas siete lámparas son los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que vigilan toda la tierra.

fr.L: Car qui a méprisé le jour des petites choses ? Ils se réjouiront et verront la pierre d’étain dans la main de Zorobabel. Ces sept [sont] les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; ils parcourent toute la terre.
fr.B: Qui a méprisé le jour des modestes débuts ? On se réjouira en voyant le fil à plomb dans la main de Zorobabel. Ces sept sont les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui parcourent toute la terre.
fr.R: Certains ont méprisé ce travail parce qu’il commençait si petit. Mais ils se réjouiront en voyant Zorobabel tenir le fil à plomb. Ces sept lampes sont les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui surveillent toute la terre.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni nani aliyeidharau siku ya mambo madogo? Watafurahi na kuliona jiwe la bati mkononi mwa Zerubabeli. Hizi saba [ni] macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; yanazunguka katika dunia yote.
sw.B: Ni nani aliyeidharau siku ya mwanzo mdogo? Watu watafurahi watakapoliona jiwe la timazi mkononi mwa Zerubabeli. Hizi saba ni macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yanayozunguka dunia yote.
sw.R: Watu wengine walidharau kazi hii kwa sababu ilianza kidogo sana. Lakini watafurahi watakapomwona Zerubabeli ameshika timazi. Taa hizi saba ni macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yanayotazama dunia yote.

vi.L: Vì ai đã khinh dể ngày của những việc nhỏ? Họ sẽ vui mừng và thấy hòn đá thiếc trong tay Xô-rô-ba-bên. Bảy [ngọn] này [là] mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; chúng đi khắp cả trái đất.
vi.B: Ai đã khinh thường ngày của những khởi đầu nhỏ bé? Người ta sẽ vui mừng khi thấy quả dọi trong tay Xô-rô-ba-bên. Bảy ngọn đèn này là mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, soi xét khắp cả trái đất.
vi.R: Có người đã coi thường công việc vì nó khởi đầu quá nhỏ bé. Nhưng họ sẽ vui mừng khi thấy Xô-rô-ba-bên cầm quả dọi trong tay. Bảy ngọn đèn này là mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nhìn khắp cả trái đất.

ko.L: 누가 작은 일들의 날을 멸시하였느냐? 그들이 스룹바벨의 손에 있는 주석 돌을 보고 기뻐할 것이다. 이 일곱은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이니, 온 땅을 두루 살핀다.
ko.B: 작은 시작의 날을 누가 멸시하였느냐? 사람들이 스룹바벨의 손에 있는 다림추를 보고 기뻐할 것이다. 이 일곱은 온 땅을 두루 살피는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람들은 시작이 너무 작다고 이 일을 하찮게 여겼다. 그러나 그들은 스룹바벨이 다림추를 들고 있는 것을 보면 기뻐할 것이다. 이 일곱 등잔은 온 땅을 살펴보시는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이다.

decisions.choice: the day of small things: a time of small beginnings
decisions.reason: The new temple seemed nothing compared with Solomon's (Haggai 2:3), and older people who had seen the first temple wept when its foundation was laid (Ezra 3:12). The question rebukes those who looked down on the work because it was small.

decisions.choice: they will rejoice: those who despised the small beginnings will rejoice when they see the work going on
alternatives: these seven, the eyes of the LORD, will rejoice when they see the stone in Zerubbabel's hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be divided in two ways. The verbs "rejoice" and "see" may have as their subject the people who despised the work: they will change their minds. Or "these seven" may be the subject: the LORD's eyes will see the work with joy. The main division of the Hebrew falls after "Zerubbabel", which favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: the tin stone: a builder's plumb weight
alternatives: an inscribed tin or lead tablet for the foundation
decisions.reason: The second word usually means tin (Numbers 31:22; Ezekiel 22:18), so the phrase is "the stone, the tin". It is most often read as a plumb weight of tin or lead hanging from a line, used to check that a wall is straight. Zerubbabel holding it means that he is in charge of the building. The same letters can mean "separation" or "chosen", and some read a stone set apart for the building, or a metal tablet laid in the foundation.

decisions.choice: these seven are the eyes of the LORD: the seven lamps show God's watchful care over all the earth
decisions.reason: "These seven" are the seven lamps of verse 2. The angel explains them as the LORD's eyes, which see everything. 2 Chronicles 16:9 says the same: "the eyes of the LORD range throughout the whole earth to strengthen those whose heart is true to him". The seven eyes on the stone in 3:9 seem to be the same.

decisions.choice: Some people looked down on the work because it began so small (R); These seven lamps (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement of what it means and says "lamps", since "these seven" points back to the seven lamps. Balanced says "plumb stone" for the tin stone (m3), and Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: "la piedra de estaño" (L), "la plomada" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew words "stone" and "tin"; Balanced and Readable name the builder's plumb weight that they most likely mean (m3).

decisions.choice: "la pierre d'étain" (L), "le fil à plomb" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tin"; the other levels name the plumb weight (m3), with the term sheet's "fil à plomb" (Amos 7:7-8).

decisions.choice: "jiwe la bati" (L), "jiwe la timazi" (B), "timazi" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tin"; the other levels name the plumb weight with "timazi", the word of Amos 7:7 and 2 Kings 21:13 (m3).

decisions.choice: "hòn đá thiếc" (L), "quả dọi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tin"; the other levels name the builder's plumb weight, the "dây dọi" of Amos 7:7 (m3).

decisions.choice: "주석 돌" (L), "다림추" (B, R); "살펴보시는" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tin", and the other levels name the plumb weight of the 다림줄 (Amos 7:7-8). Readable gives the LORD's eyes the honorific, since the angel speaks about God.

source.text: וָאַ֖עַן וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְּׁנֵ֤י הַזֵּיתִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶה עַל־יְמִ֥ין הַמְּנוֹרָ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂמֹאולָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I answered and said to him, What [are] the two olive trees the these on the right of the lampstand and on its left?

en.L: And I answered and said to him, "What [are] these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
en.B: Then I asked him, "What are these two olive trees to the right and left of the lampstand?"
en.R: Then I asked the angel, "What are these two olive trees, one on the right side of the lampstand and one on the left?"

es.L: Y respondí y le dije: «¿Qué [son] estos dos olivos a la derecha del candelabro y a su izquierda?».
es.B: Entonces le pregunté: «¿Qué son estos dos olivos a la derecha y a la izquierda del candelabro?».
es.R: Entonces le pregunté al ángel: «¿Qué son estos dos olivos, uno a la derecha del candelabro y otro a la izquierda?».

fr.L: Et je pris la parole et lui dis : « Que [sont] ces deux oliviers à droite du chandelier et à sa gauche ? »
fr.B: Alors je lui demandai : « Que sont ces deux oliviers à droite et à gauche du chandelier ? »
fr.R: Ensuite, j’ai demandé à l’ange : « Que sont ces deux oliviers, l’un à droite du chandelier et l’autre à gauche ? »

sw.L: Nikajibu, nikamwambia, "Mizeituni hii miwili iliyo upande wa kuume wa kinara cha taa na upande wake wa kushoto ni nini?"
sw.B: Kisha nikamwuliza, "Mizeituni hii miwili iliyo kuume na kushoto kwa kinara cha taa ni nini?"
sw.R: Kisha nikamwuliza malaika, "Mizeituni hii miwili, mmoja upande wa kuume wa kinara cha taa na mwingine upande wa kushoto, ni nini?"

vi.L: Tôi đáp và nói với người: "Hai cây ô-liu này ở bên phải chân đèn và bên trái nó [là] gì?"
vi.B: Bấy giờ tôi hỏi thiên sứ: "Hai cây ô-liu ở bên phải và bên trái chân đèn này là gì?"
vi.R: Bấy giờ tôi hỏi thiên sứ: "Hai cây ô-liu này, một cây bên phải chân đèn và một cây bên trái, là gì vậy?"

ko.L: 그래서 내가 그에게 대답하여 말하였다. "등잔대 오른쪽과 그 왼쪽에 있는 이 두 올리브나무는 무엇입니까?"
ko.B: 그때 내가 그에게 물었다. "등잔대 오른쪽과 왼쪽에 있는 이 두 올리브나무는 무엇입니까?"
ko.R: 그때 내가 천사에게 물었다. "등잔대 오른쪽에 하나, 왼쪽에 하나 있는 이 두 올리브나무는 무엇입니까?"

decisions.choice: Zechariah asks again: the vision resumes
decisions.reason: The angel has explained the seven lamps, but not the trees. Zechariah asks about them twice (verses 11 and 12), the second time more precisely.

decisions.choice: the angel (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the angel for "him", since the word to Zerubbabel has come between.

source.text: וָאַ֣עַן שֵׁנִ֔ית וָאֹמַ֖ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְׁתֵּ֞י שִׁבֲּלֵ֣י הַזֵּיתִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּיַ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ צַנְתְּר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֔ב הַֽמְרִיקִ֥ים מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And I answered a second [time] and said to him, What [are the] two branches of the olive trees which [are] beside [the] two pipes of the gold, which empty out from them the gold?

en.L: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What [are] the two branches of the olive trees that [are] beside the two golden pipes, which pour out from themselves the gold?"
en.B: I asked him again, "What are the two branches of the olive trees beside the two gold pipes that pour out the golden oil?"
en.R: I asked him again, "What are the two olive branches beside the two gold pipes? Golden oil is pouring out through them."

es.L: Y respondí por segunda vez y le dije: «¿Qué [son] las dos ramas de los olivos que [están] junto a los dos tubos de oro, que vierten de sí el oro?».
es.B: Le pregunté otra vez: «¿Qué son las dos ramas de los olivos que están junto a los dos tubos de oro que derraman el aceite dorado?».
es.R: Le pregunté otra vez: «¿Qué son las dos ramas de olivo que están junto a los dos tubos de oro? Por ellos sale aceite dorado».

fr.L: Et je pris la parole une seconde fois et lui dis : « Que [sont] les deux rameaux des oliviers qui [sont] à côté des deux conduits d’or, qui déversent d’eux-mêmes l’or ? »
fr.B: Je lui demandai encore : « Que sont les deux rameaux des oliviers à côté des deux conduits d’or qui déversent l’huile dorée ? »
fr.R: Je lui ai demandé encore : « Que sont les deux rameaux d’olivier à côté des deux conduits d’or ? De l’huile dorée s’en écoule. »

sw.L: Nikajibu mara ya pili, nikamwambia, "Matawi haya mawili ya mizeituni yaliyo kando ya mirija miwili ya dhahabu, inayomimina dhahabu kutoka ndani yake, ni nini?"
sw.B: Nikamwuliza tena, "Matawi mawili ya mizeituni yaliyo kando ya mirija miwili ya dhahabu inayomimina mafuta ya rangi ya dhahabu ni nini?"
sw.R: Nikamwuliza tena, "Matawi haya mawili ya mizeituni yaliyo kando ya mirija miwili ya dhahabu ni nini? Mafuta ya rangi ya dhahabu yanatiririka kupitia mirija hiyo."

vi.L: Tôi đáp lần thứ hai và nói với người: "Hai nhánh ô-liu ở bên cạnh hai ống bằng vàng, là những ống đổ vàng ra từ chính nó, [là] gì?"
vi.B: Tôi lại hỏi thiên sứ: "Hai nhánh ô-liu bên cạnh hai ống vàng đang đổ dầu vàng óng ra là gì?"
vi.R: Tôi lại hỏi thiên sứ: "Hai nhánh ô-liu bên cạnh hai ống vàng là gì? Dầu vàng óng đang chảy ra qua hai ống ấy."

ko.L: 내가 두 번째로 대답하여 그에게 말하였다. "자기에게서 금을 쏟아 내는 두 금 대롱 곁에 있는 올리브나무의 두 가지는 무엇입니까?"
ko.B: 내가 다시 그에게 물었다. "금빛 기름을 쏟아 내는 두 금 대롱 곁에 있는 올리브나무의 두 가지는 무엇입니까?"
ko.R: 내가 다시 그에게 물었다. "두 금 대롱 곁에 있는 올리브나무 두 가지는 무엇입니까? 그 대롱으로 금빛 기름이 흘러나오고 있습니다."

decisions.choice: branches: olive branches heavy with fruit
decisions.reason: The word usually means an ear of grain (Genesis 41:5). Here it is used of the olive trees, so it seems to mean a fruit-laden branch or cluster from which the oil comes.

decisions.choice: pipes: channels carrying oil from the trees to the lampstand
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It seems to mean a pipe or channel, perhaps the spouts of a press. The picture is of oil flowing from the trees, through gold pipes, into the bowl of the lampstand, without any human hand.

decisions.choice: the gold: the golden oil
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that the pipes "pour out the gold". Fresh olive oil is golden in color, and the word is used for the oil that is golden like the lampstand.

decisions.choice: the golden oil (B); Golden oil (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "oil", which the context makes plain (m3). Readable splits the question into a question and a statement.

decisions.choice: "ramas"; "tubos de oro"; "el oro" (L), "el aceite dorado" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the gold" for the golden oil, as the Hebrew does (m3); Balanced and Readable add "aceite", as the English adds "oil".

decisions.choice: "가지"; "금 대롱"; "금" (L), "금빛 기름" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the gold" (m3); the other levels say golden oil. 대롱 names the pipes that carry the oil (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, saying, Do not you know what these [are]? And I said, No, my lord.

en.L: And he said to me, "Do you not know what these [are]?" And I said, "No, my lord."
en.B: He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" "No, my lord," I answered.
en.R: He said, "Do you not know what these are?" "No, my lord," I answered.

decisions.choice: the two sons of fresh oil: two people set apart by anointing
alternatives: two who are full of oil
decisions.reason: "Son of" a thing means one who belongs to it or is marked by it. Kings and priests were anointed with oil when they took office (Exodus 29:7; 1 Samuel 16:13), so "sons of oil" are most likely two anointed leaders. The word here is the one for fresh oil, not the usual word for anointing oil, so some read "the two who supply oil". The angel does not name them. In the book's setting they are most often taken as Joshua the high priest and Zerubbabel, the heir of David, the two leaders named in chapters 3 and 4; together they serve the LORD as his chosen leaders.

decisions.choice: the Lord of all the earth: God as ruler of the whole world
decisions.reason: The title is used of God in Joshua 3:11, 13, Micah 4:13 and Psalm 97:5. It fits the visions, in which the LORD's eyes and riders go through all the earth.

decisions.choice: Revelation 11:4: the two witnesses are "the two olive trees and the two lampstands"
decisions.reason: Revelation takes up this vision for the two witnesses who prophesy in the last days and stand "before the Lord of the earth".

decisions.choice: sons of fresh oil (L); anointed ones (B); who have been anointed with oil (R); Lord, capitalized
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew expression; Balanced and Readable give its likely sense (m1). The Lord here is God, so the word is capitalized, as set for the word "lord" used of God, and Readable's "his" takes the setting for pronouns of God.

decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording: Literal keeps the Hebrew expression and the other levels give its likely sense (m1). "Señor" is capitalized because God is meant (m2), and Readable's "su" takes the pronoun setting, as the English "his".

decisions.choice: "les deux fils de l'huile fraîche" (L), "les deux oints" (B); "le Seigneur de toute la terre"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for 4:14; "Seigneur" with a capital, since God is meant; the two anointed take no pronoun setting.
